about.title: About Us
about.missionText: To provide excellent advice and service by offering our products to the hardware and construction sectors, under standards of variety, quality, and best price; satisfying the needs of our customers.
about.visionText: To be recognized as the leading company in the steel and hardware sector for our profitability, quality of products and services, in order to raise the standard of living of our workers.
about.companyText: Founded in 1963 by Mr. Giovanni Ricupero Lombardi (deceased) and Mrs. María Stallone de Ricupero, established from the very beginning in the facilities we currently operate, Ciudad Bolívar, Bolívar State, with various renovations, expansions, and modernizations adapted over these more than 60 years.
about.testimonial1Text: A solid strategic alliance has been developed over time between HIERROS RICUPERO, C.A. and our company BELIS GROUP, C.A. with the timely supply of high-quality materials at very competitive prices, which allows us to meet our main objective of strengthening the construction and design industry with the use of new technologies, meeting the requirements of our customers with the highest quality levels.
about.testimonial2Text: For the success of any Civil and Industrial Engineering project, it is important to have adequate and quality supplies. Constru Hierros Ricupero has provided us with the security and proper advice to ensure the fulfillment of activities, with maximum performance at the best cost in the shortest possible time. In this way, we have managed to create a competitive team, creating a bond of trust and security which is reflected in the great satisfaction of our customers.
about.testimonial3Text: The service offered by Constru-ir fills us with satisfaction as customers because it is characterized by its quick attention, the products have excellent price and quality, and above all, the pre-sale advice makes everything easier.

terms.intro: These terms govern purchases made through this online store. Please read them before placing an order.

If you disagree with any of them, do not complete the purchase: write to us first and we will talk it through.

cuenta.title: Registration and user account
body: You can buy as a guest, without opening an account, or you can register. If you buy as a guest, the store still keeps your details in a record tied to your ID document: the privacy policy explains this.
If you do choose to register, registration asks for an email address that must be verified: until you confirm the link we send you, the account cannot sign in.
list: You are responsible for the data you register being true and up to date.
You are responsible for your password and for whatever is done from your account.
We may deactivate an account [TO BE DEFINED: in which cases and with how much prior notice].
[TO BE DEFINED: how a customer closes their own account; the store offers no such option today and it has to be handled by hand]

productos.title: Products, stock and presentation
body: Each product is published with the description, photos and availability held in our system.
Stock is checked when the order is confirmed: a product showing in the catalogue does not guarantee there will be stock left when you pay.
list: Photos are for reference; colour, presentation or brand may differ between batches.
[TO BE DEFINED: what is done about an obvious description or price error spotted after an order is placed, and whether the customer is told before going on]

precios.title: Prices, VAT and exchange rate
body: Catalogue prices include VAT. Checkout breaks out the taxable base and the VAT, but the total you pay is the same one you saw in the catalogue.
Prices are kept in US dollars and the bolívar amount is worked out with the official Central Bank of Venezuela rate held in the system.
list: The VAT rate depends on each product's type; some products are exempt.
The BCV rate updates automatically, so the bolívar amount of the same order can change from one day to the next.
[TO BE DEFINED: which rate applies when the order is placed one day and paid on another: the order's or the payment's]
[TO BE DEFINED: how long the price of an unpaid order is honoured]

pedido.title: How an order is placed
body: You add products to the cart, choose store pickup or delivery, give the delivery details and pick a payment method. Once sent, the order is recorded with a number you can use to track it.
A submitted order is a purchase request. [TO BE DEFINED: at which moment the sale is considered closed: on submitting the order, on verifying payment, or on dispatch]
We may decline an order. [TO BE DEFINED: grounds on which the store may reject an order]

pago.title: Payment methods and receipts
body: We accept Zelle, mobile payment and bank transfer. After paying you must report the payment from the store, uploading the receipt and the reference number.
The order does not move forward until we verify the payment with the bank.
list: The receipt must match the amount and the order; an incomplete payment leaves the order on hold.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: This page explains what data of yours this store collects, what it is used for and who it is shared with. It was written from what the system actually does, not from a generic template.
privacy.contactIntro: To ask about your data, correct it or request that we delete it, write to us:

responsable.title: Who handles your data
body: The data you give this store is handled by the business whose contact details appear at the end of this document.
[TO BE DEFINED: legal name, tax ID (RIF) and registered address of the data controller]
[TO BE DEFINED: specific email or person to address data protection requests to]

alcance.title: What this policy covers
body: This policy describes what the store's system does with your data today: it was written by going through the program itself, field by field.
It does not cover what other sites we link to do — social networks, WhatsApp, maps — nor what happens in the physical store outside this website.

datosCuenta.title: Data we ask for when you open an account
body: You can browse the catalogue without identifying yourself. If you register, we store:
list: First and last name.
Email address, which must be verified through a link we send you.
Phone number.
Type and number of your ID document (V, E, J, G or P): national ID, tax ID or passport.
Password, stored hashed with bcrypt: nobody at the store can read it.
Alongside that, the date you created the account, whether it is active and whether the email was verified.

datosPedido.title: Data from each order
body: When you buy, we store with the order whatever is needed to prepare and deliver it:
list: First name, last name, email and phone of the person receiving it.
Type and number of the ID document.
Delivery address: street, city, state, postal code, country and extra directions.
If you mark your location on the map, the exact coordinates — latitude and longitude — of the point you pick.
Any notes you write on the order.
The products, quantities and amounts, which over time build up your purchase history.
Internal notes store staff may write about the order.
If you are signed in, whatever you leave in the cart is stored on your account even if you do not finish the purchase.

If you buy without an account, that same data is kept in a record tied to your ID number, along with how many orders you have placed and the date of the last one. It is used so that on your next purchase, typing your ID number fills in your name, email, phone and address for you.

datosPago.title: Payment data
body: Payments are verified by hand: there is no payment gateway, so the store never receives or stores card numbers. Depending on the method you use, we store:
list: Zelle: name of the sender and bank.
Mobile payment: phone, ID number, bank and reference number.
Bank transfer: account holder's name, bank and reference number.
The receipt you upload — image or PDF — stored on Amazon S3, and the outcome of its review.

The receipt is stored under a name nobody could guess, but the store does not serve it through temporary links. [TO BE DEFINED: confirm with whoever administers the Amazon storage that the receipts folder does not allow public reads, and state it here]

datosTecnicos.title: Data collected on its own as you browse
body: Even if you fill in no form, simply browsing records:
list: Every page you visit, with its title, the page you came from, your IP address and your browser's identifier. That is stored in our own database, one row per visit.
If the integration is switched on, Google Analytics also records the pages you view, along with whatever Google collects on its own account.

Requests from the integration with the store's back-office system are logged with the path, the request contents — which on an order include your contact and delivery details — the IP and the browser. Passwords and keys are replaced with asterisks before being stored.
None of this asks your permission first today: the store has no cookie notice. [TO BE DEFINED: whether a cookie notice with prior consent will be added; worth checking with a lawyer]

cookies.title: Cookies and data kept in your browser
body: The following is stored in your own browser, not on our servers:
list: token: your signed-in session, in a cookie lasting seven days. A copy is also kept in the browser's local storage.
user: your basic details — name, surname, email and role — in local storage, so they need not be fetched on every screen.
cart: your cart, when you shop without an account.

checkout_draft: the checkout draft while you fill it in, so it is not lost if you reload. It is cleared when the order is confirmed and when the tab is closed. It includes the password if you ticked create an account.
NEXT_LOCALE: the language you chose, for one year.
Google Analytics cookies, if that integration is switched on.
Signing out clears the session and your basic details; the rest goes when you clear the site's data in your browser.

finalidades.title: What we use your data for
body: Every piece of data we ask for has a specific use:
list: Preparing your order, verifying your payment and delivering it or holding it for pickup.
Sending you the emails about your purchase: order received, payment verified or rejected, order dispatched or ready for pickup.
Sending you the emails about your account: email verification, password reset and welcome.
Letting store staff know a new order has come in.
Handling your questions and complaints.
Knowing which pages get visited, so we can improve the store.
Meeting the tax and accounting obligations of a sale.

We do not use your data for advertising and we do not sell it to anyone. The subscription form in the footer is not connected to any service yet: today it sends your address nowhere and subscribes you to no list.

terceros.title: Who it is shared with
body: We do not sell your data. It is shared only with whoever is needed for the purchase to work:
list: Amazon Web Services: stores the payment receipt you upload.
The outgoing email provider: receives your address and the contents of the messages we send you. [TO BE DEFINED: name of the email provider used in production]

The store's back-office system: receives each order with the name, ID document, address, city, email and phone, in order to invoice and dispatch it. It can also pull the full customer list and search it by name or email, not only the customers on a given order. [TO BE DEFINED: name of the company operating that system and under what agreement it handles the data]
Google Analytics, if that integration is switched on, with whatever Google collects on its own account.
OpenStreetMap: if you use the map to mark your address, your browser requests the map tiles directly and that service sees your IP and the area you are looking at.
Other systems connected through automatic notifications, which receive orders and customers as they are created or changed. [TO BE DEFINED: which systems are connected today and what for]
The authorities, where the law requires it.
Several of these services are outside Venezuela, so your data is processed and stored abroad.

conservacion.title: How long it is kept
body: Plainly: today the system deletes nothing on its own. There is no automatic clean-up, so your account, your orders, your addresses, your receipts and the browsing logs are kept indefinitely.
When an account is deleted from the back office, it is marked as deleted but the information stays in the database.

[TO BE DEFINED: retention period for each kind of data — account, orders and receipts, browsing and request logs — and how they will be purged. None of it is implemented: any period written here before it is built would be a promise with nothing behind it]

seguridad.title: How it is protected
body: These are the measures the system has today, stated without embellishment:
list: Passwords are stored hashed with bcrypt; nobody at the store can read them.
Getting into the back office requires signing in, and each internal user has permissions according to their role.
Passwords and keys are masked before being written to the request logs.
Looking up a buyer's details by ID number is limited to a few times per minute.
No system is infallible. [TO BE DEFINED: how and within what time frame affected people will be notified if unauthorised access to their data is detected]

derechos.title: Your rights and how to exercise them
body: You can ask us to access your data, correct it, update it or delete it.
It matters that you know what you can do yourself today and what has to be requested, because the store does not have screens for everything yet:
list: You can see your orders and the detail of each one from My account.
You can track an order with its number, without signing in.
You can reset your password if you forgot it, and sign out whenever you want.
There is no screen yet to edit your name or email, nor to change your password while signed in: you have to ask us.
Phone number and ID number cannot be changed from the store; staff correct them.
There is no way yet to delete your account or download your data from the store: it is done by hand when you ask.
Cancelling an order also has to be requested; the online store does not allow it on your own.
[TO BE DEFINED: time frame within which the store commits to answering a data protection request]

menores.title: Minors
body: This store is meant for adults. Today the system neither asks nor checks the age of whoever buys.
[TO BE DEFINED: minimum age required to buy and what is done if a minor's account is found]

cambios.title: Changes to this policy
body: If what the system does with your data changes, this page must change with it: it describes the program, not an ideal.
[TO BE DEFINED: whether changes will be announced and through which channel]
